_README: VENDORED copies of sigzen_lead's normalisers -- sigzen_ai_scan_crm_connector must not import sigzen_lead,
because it is installed on client sites where sigzen_lead does not exist.
Copies drift. This file is the contract that stops them: sigzen_ai_scan_crm_connector reads it in
tests/test_normalisers.py, and sigzen_lead is expected to grow the twin test reading THE
SAME file, so a change made on one side and not the other fails a test in that repo.
Until that twin test exists in sigzen_lead, only the sigzen_ai_scan_crm_connector side is pinned.
The sections below `phone_match_keys` are sigzen_ai_scan_crm_connector's OWN -- phone_match_key and
storable_phones have no twin in sigzen_lead and are not part of the drift contract. They
exist because the vendored match key keeps only the last ten digits (so two numbers that
differ only in country code collapse into one) and says nothing about whether a value can
be STORED on a Contact Phone row at all.
`storable_emails` is sigzen_ai_scan_crm_connector's own too, and for the same reason as storable_phones:
one legacy field can hold two addresses, and validate_email_address alone says yes to

storable_phones._why: The real number is 22 characters, which frappe's 20-character PHONE_STORAGE_PATTERN refuses. Nothing storable may be invented from what is left: the 'ext 9' run used to win a max() fallback and be written to the client's Contact as their phone number.
Two whole numbers written as one run. Splitting at a bracket that opens a full number recovers both; before, the 22-character run was refused entire and neither number reached the Contact.
A bracketed trunk code is NOT a second number, so this does not split: it stays one unstorable value and goes to the note as printed.
Every run is short, so the value really is one short number (a desk extension) rather than a number plus an annotation.

storable_emails._why: TWO addresses in one legacy field. frappe.utils.validate_email_address is truthy for the whole string and Contact Email stores it verbatim, so the migration used to write one row neither address could be found in.
A display-name form. validate_email_address returns the address out of the angle brackets, which is truthy, so the whole string used to be stored as the address.
Semicolons separate addresses too, and case is normalised on the way in.
A scan that is not an address at all: nothing is stored and the value as printed goes to the tagged note.
